syllabusTopics: Limits and continuity: limits of a function, indeterminate forms, algebraic properties of limits (without proof), basic theorems on limits of algebraic, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions
Continuity of a function, types of discontinuity, graphs of discontinuous function
Derivatives: derivative of a function, derivatives of algebraic, trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions by definition (simple forms)
Rules of differentiation; derivatives of parametric and implicit functions; higher order derivatives
Geometric interpretation of derivative; monotonicity of a function, interval of monotonicity, extreme values of a function, concavity, points of inflection
Anti-derivatives: integration using basic integrals, integration by substitution and by parts methods
The definite integral; the definite integral as an area under the given curve; area between two curves

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The self-replicating base*** - e^x is the unique function equal to its own derivative: the (e^h - 1)/h -> 1 star is the whole story of why e rules calculus.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Extended Derivative Table **Derivatives of inverse trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions** — completing the standard table that every chain-rule computation consumes.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Inverse trigonometric derivatives - **d/dx sin⁻¹x = 1/√(1 − x²)** (|x| < 1); **d/dx cos⁻¹x = −1/√(1 − x²)**; **d/dx tan⁻¹x = 1/(1 + x²)**; **d/dx cot⁻¹x = −1/(1 + x²)**; **d/dx sec⁻¹x = 1/(|x|√(x² − 1))**; **d/dx cosec⁻¹x = −1/(|x|√(x² − 1))**. - **Memory pattern:** co-functions carry minus signs; sin/cos and tan/cot pairs are ± of each other.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Co-functions: minus sign. tan^-1: no absolute value needed. a^x: multiply by ln a. Chain rule: outer table + inner derivative.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2020 (verified PYQ): d/dx [log_a(sin x)] equals: (choose the correct option). (1m)** — **Chain rule, outer first:** the outer function is log_a(u) with u = sin x; its derivative is 1/(u ln a) (the general-base log derivative, carrying the ln a tax). **Inner:** (sin x)′ = cos x.…  ·  **NEB 2022 (verified PYQ): Find dy/dx for y = ln(sin x). (3m)** — **Chain rule:** the outer function is ln(u) with derivative 1/u; the inner is u = sin x with derivative cos x. **Compose:** dy/dx = (1/sin x)·cos x = **cos x/sin x = cot x**.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: For MCQs on log_a(sin x)-type derivatives, compute the chain rule fully then match - do not pattern-match partially differentiated options.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The inverse-engine rule (f^-1)' = 1/f' derives the entire inverse-trig table from the trig table - one theorem, six derivatives.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Inverse trig derivatives: (sin^-1 x)' = 1/sqrt(1-x^2); (cos^-1 x)' = -1/sqrt(1-x^2); (tan^-1 x)' = 1/(1+x^2); (cot^-1 x)' = -1/(1+x^2); (sec^-1 x)' = 1/(|x| sqrt(x^2-1)); (cosec^-1 x)' = -1/(|x| sqrt(x^2-1)). Co-functions carry minus signs.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Population growth and radioactive decay are a^t curves; only e^t has growth rate proportional to itself with constant 1 - nature's default is e.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Differentiate (i) y = tan⁻¹(3x), (ii) y = e^{−x²}.** — **(i)** Outer: (tan⁻¹u)′ = 1/(1 + u²); inner u = 3x, u′ = 3. Compose: dy/dx = **3/(1 + 9x²)** — the coefficient lands in both numerator and inside the square.…  ·  **NEB-style (5m): Derive d/dx (sin⁻¹x) = 1/√(1 − x²) using the inverse-function relation, stating the domain carefully.** — **Setup:** let y = sin⁻¹x, so x = sin y with y ∈ [−π/2, π/2] (the principal branch — this is what makes the inverse a *function*).…  ·  **NEB-style (5m): Using first principles, prove that d/dx (aˣ) = aˣ ln a, and deduce the derivative of eˣ.** — **Definition:** f′(x) = lim_{h→0} [a^{x+h} − aˣ]/h = lim aˣ·[aʰ − 1]/h = **aˣ · lim_{h→0} (aʰ − 1)/h** (the constant aˣ factors out — the constant-multiple limit theorem).…

Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why e is the natural base - (eˣ)′ = eˣ means the exponential's rate equals its value — self-replication. Every other base pays the ln a tax. This uniqueness is why calculus is written in e.…  ·  ## 5. rows.text: **NEB-style (5m): Differentiate y = tan⁻¹((1 + x)/(1 − x)) and simplify the result.** — **Chain rule, outer first:** with u = (1+x)/(1−x), dy/dx = [1/(1 + u²)]·u′. **Inner derivative (quotient rule):** u′ = [(1)(1−x) − (1+x)(−1)]/(1−x)² = [1 − x + 1 + x]/(1−x)² = **2/(1−x)²**.…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): Differentiate y = (tan x)^{x} using logarithmic differentiation, and state where the method is mandatory.** — **Why mandatory:** both base (tan x) and exponent (x) vary — the power rule needs a constant exponent, the exponential rule a constant base; neither applies alone.…  ·  Differentiate ln(sin x).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Limit to remember: derivative f'(x) = lim_{h→0} [f(x+h) − f(x)]/h = tangent slope; rules: sum, product, quotient, chain.  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **The ± pattern:** cos⁻¹, cot⁻¹, cosec⁻¹ all carry minus signs — forgetting the sign flips the answer.  ·  **(aˣ)′ ≠ x·aˣ⁻¹:** that is the power rule for variable base, constant exponent — aˣ has constant base, variable exponent and needs ln a.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Domains:** sin⁻¹/cos⁻¹ formulas need |x| < 1 (interior of the domain); sec⁻¹/cosec⁻¹ need |x| > 1.  ·  ## 7. Exam Application **NEB 2020 (verified PYQ): d/dx [log_a(sin x)] equals: (a) 1/(sin x·log_e a) (b) cot x/... (MCQ, 1m)** — **Chain rule:** d/dx log_a(sin x) = [1/(sin x·ln a)]·cos x = **cot x/ln a**. Compare with the options: the form matching cot x/(ln a) — i.e.…  ·  **NEB 2022 (verified PYQ): Find dy/dx for y = ln(sin x). (3m)** — **Chain rule:** dy/dx = (1/sin x)·d/dx(sin x) = (1/sin x)·cos x = **cot x**. (Equivalently: ln(sin x) = ln|sin x| on the domain sin x > 0; the derivative is cot x wherever defined.)
